capabilities.name: Wall / Door / Window / Column / Slab instance recovery from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records + partition_schema_mvp::instances_from_partition_category_records / slabs_from_partition_category_records + partition_ifc_export_overrides; tests/project_count_fixtures.rs (IFCWALL 360/360, IFCDOOR 132/132, IFCWINDOW 6/6, IFCCOLUMN 256/256, IFCSLAB 80/80, IFCSHADINGDEVICE 20/20, tolerance 0) and the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict, where entity_counts.IFCWALL / IFCDOOR / IFCWINDOW / IFCCOLUMN / IFCSLAB / IFCSHADINGDEVICE are all inside the claimed surface and rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell and IFClite agree exactly
capabilities.notes: Scope is six BuiltInCategories (OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Windows, OST_Columns, OST_Floors, OST_BuildingPad), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. Selection is a direct byte test, not a heuristic: the record must carry no container reference at +0x32 and placement kind 0xffffef7f at +0x42 (RE-21). It supersedes the #204 column rule, whose family-local bbox proxy and highest-ElementId-per-footprint collapse are removed. RE-22 (#212) extended the same rule to slabs and found it already exact there: its 99 OST_Floors selections are all exported (79 IfcSlab + 20 IfcShadingDevice), and the 80th exported slab is an OST_BuildingPad (Pad:Site Pad, ElementId 21975). The IfcSlab / IfcShadingDevice split is a per-instance Revit 'IFC Export As' override read out of the partition parameter block: the UTF-16LE value string with the owning ElementId as a u64 at -0x0dc and again at -0x11e, both required to agree and to be declared in Global/ElemTable. Thirty-one entries pass on this file, naming 21 ids; the 20 that are also placed instances are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set. Only IfcShadingDevice is honoured as an override target — an unrecognised value leaves the element on its class mapping. Where one ElementId is framed more than once, the record with the greatest bounding-box z extent is kept; that agrees with the export's IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.Depth on 79 of 80 slabs (the 80th is exported as two stacked solids summing to it). Ties go to the newest frame - the greatest (stream, offset) - because Revit rewrites an edited element into a higher-numbered Partitions stream and leaves the earlier copy in place (RE-26): 171 of 360 walls and 96 of 132 doors carry two frames that disagree about the plan box, and on the newest one the wall's thin plan extent equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 (201 of 360 on the oldest) and its type slot equals that IfcWallType.Tag on 356 of 360 (183 of 360 on the oldest; the positional read is superseded by RE-28's set test, which is 360 of 360 - see element-record-wall-type-join). Global/ElemTable's u32 at +0x1c is a monotone version counter that ranks the same way across all 976 exported instances. No frame of any instance on this file disagrees about the box's z, so the tie-break cannot move an element between storeys - storey_bound_elements was 801 either way when this was measured, and is 853 since #219 / RE-27. Column, window, slab and building-pad boxes are unchanged; door boxes move without a measurement that adjudicates them, since a door's record box is not the panel Revit exports and 0 of 132 are world-exact either way. Bodies are the record's own bounding box, not a recovered family profile or wall location curve; for plates the z extent is the real thickness, and since RE-25 (#31) the plan profile of a slab whose sketch closes is the recovered sketch boundary rather than the box rectangle - see element-record-slab-plan-profile. Base/top Level ElementIds stay unbound (#86); doors and windows are attached to their host wall as of RE-23/#222 (see element-record-door-window-host-binding). Storey containment came from the #213 column-derived elevation set when this row landed: walls, doors and columns bound by their record base, plates by their record top face (Revit hangs a floor below its level) — 51 of 100 plates bound and all 51 agreed with the export, none wrongly, while windows never bound because their record base is a sill height, measured 0 of 6. Since #219 / RE-27 the first join tried is the Level ElementId the record itself names, which reaches all 100 plates and all 6 windows; that elevation path survives as the fallback - see record-level-reference-storey-bind. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: On the recorded Revit 2024 project, walls, doors, windows, architectural columns, floor slabs and building pads come out as placed IFC entities with position, a solid body and (for slabs) a measured thickness and plan profile, matching Revit's own export element for element. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers 2024 samples most element frames use a second prologue; their ElementIds come from the enclosing partition record (RE-35), and walls, doors, windows, columns and floors export under Revit's own ids (see element-records-second-prologue-ids). Structural framing, structural columns, foundations and generic models export from the same records (see element-records-structural-categories).

capabilities.name: Revit 2026 partition element records, with storeys, rooms, doors and windows, type names and layer sets
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::BBOX_MARKER_2026 and file_bbox_marker; partition_level_records::elevation_marker; partition_names::ELEMENT_DATA_HEADER_2026; partition_compound_structure::layer_layout; partition_materials (2026 tags); probes/examples/probe_re124_revit_2026_records.rs; tools/re/instances_vs_ifc_tags.py; reports/element-framing/RE-124-revit-2026-element-records.md
capabilities.notes: Measured on one Revit 2026 project, the flowbim.ee single-dwelling house (local only), against Revit 26.4's own IFC4X3 export. Every per-release constant is the tag of a class in the file's own schema (Outline and ElementParents for the record marker, Plane for Level elevations, CellList for element data, VerticalRegionsStructure for layers, Material, PatternHelper and PhysicalParamSet for materials); a 2026 layer record is 41 bytes, the 2025 fields at their offsets plus a repeated u32. Result: 113 of the export's 115 elements, none outside it, each in Revit's class, with Revit's GlobalId on all 113; the 4 storeys with Revit's names and elevations; 13 of 13 rooms with Revit's number and name; 13 of 13 doors and 15 of 16 windows as IfcDoor/IfcWindow in their host; walls named Family:Type as Revit's; 61 layer sets named and as thick as Revit's, with Revit's layer material names in Revit's order on all 320 layers (RE-125, RE-126), and 65 of the 67 elements given materials with Revit's set. Wall bodies are drawn along each wall's centreline and joined by its join lists (RE-126): faces Revit's on 59 of 59 and height on 37; against Revit's CoordinationView export, which draws each wall as one box, 85 of 118 ends are where it puts them. Not read on 2026: roof slopes, stairs, beam axes, IFC export overrides, opening index.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2026 projects export typed elements under Revit's ElementIds and GlobalIds, on Revit's storeys, with rooms named and doors and windows in their walls; measured on one model.

capabilities.name: Revit 2008 to 2010 partition element records, read in the 32-bit layout of Revit 2011 to 2023, with storeys and named materials
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records_2023::REVIT_32BIT_RELEASES, schema_tags and envelope_shortfall; partition_materials (name_before_properties); partition_level_records::framed_plane_marker; probes/examples/probe_re260_revit_2008_2010.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-260-revit-2008-2010-element-records.md
capabilities.notes: Revit 2009 and 2010 frame their element records as 2011 does (a declared u32 ElementId 52 bytes before every marker of the local files); Revit 2008's envelope has 12 bytes between the category and the placement kind where later releases have 16, all ff, so its id is 48 bytes before the marker. Each release takes its own tags of the five schema classes RE-180 lists, and 2011 to 2013's shading frame and value blocks (RE-259) hold on 2008 and 2009. A 2008 to 2011 material's name is a u32-counted string followed by three equal f64s, with no PhysicalParamSet tag after it: every material of the local 2008 to 2011 files is now named, and where its own MaterialElemGroupHelper frame names it too the two agree (43 of 43). A 2008 to 2012 Level's elevation follows ff ff ff ff and the Plane tag after its name, one reference slot and 16 bytes, written twice 24 bytes apart: every local 2008 to 2012 file reads its Levels as storeys (Revit's template 0 and 10 ft, and 0 and 4 m on one 2012 project). There is no Revit export and no copy of the same model saved by another release of any 2008 to 2010 file here, and every one is closed source and measured locally only; what is shown is that the records read without a byte left over and that the elements hang together (a 2009 wall and its 8 doors on two storeys, a 2008 causeway as one generic model). Not read, as on 2015 to 2023: design options, layered joins, IFC export overrides, parameters.
capabilities.user_impact: Outside the 1.0 range (2015 to 2027), measured on the contributor's local closed-source files only. Revit 2008 to 2010 projects export typed elements under Revit's ElementIds, on their storeys, with named materials; checked only for consistency within each file, not against Revit's export. Revit 2011 and 2012 projects gain their storeys and, on 2011, their material names.

capabilities.name: Revit 2011 to 2014 partition element records, read in the 32-bit layout of Revit 2015 to 2023, with storeys, hosts, type names, layer sets and materials
capabilities.evidence: basic_file_info (release years from 2008, the build-date release); formats::schema_classes (schemas without GUID lists); partition_element_records_2023::REVIT_32BIT_RELEASES and schema_tags; partition_materials::shading_ids_32; partition_type_materials (2011 to 2013 blocks that hold no map); probes/examples/probe_re259_revit_2011_2014.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-259-revit-2011-2014-element-records.md
capabilities.notes: Files written before Revit 2014 did not open: BasicFileInfo was read only for a year from 2014 on, and a schema written before 2014 has no GUID list after a class's fields. With both read, every local 2008 to 2013 file opens and its schema reads to the end; 2008 and 2009, which state no year, take the build year plus one. Revit 2011 to 2014 frame their element records as 2015 does: on eight local 2011 to 2014 files every record marker has a declared u32 ElementId 52 bytes before it. Each release takes its own tags of the five schema classes RE-180 lists. Two layouts differ from 2015's on 2011 to 2013: a material's shading frame holds two u32 ElementIds between the 0.5 and the pattern slots, and an ElementId and the value-block mark also open blocks that hold no type's map. 2011 to 2013 Levels hold the instance placement kind; 2014 Levels hold 2015's. There is no Revit export of a file before 2015, and every one measured is closed source and measured locally only: the oracle is a local copy of Autodesk's 2013 rac_advanced sample against the pinned 2015 copy. Every ElementId both hold has its class, and 62,071 of 62,153 fields agree; the rest are in the files' own records (a re-divided curtain wall, a shorter wall, two beams' Level references). 2011, 2012 and 2014 have no same-model pair. Revit 2008 to 2010 files open with their metadata and schema, and their element records are not read. Not read, as on 2015 to 2023: design options, layered joins, IFC export overrides, parameters.
capabilities.user_impact: Outside the 1.0 range (2015 to 2027), measured on the contributor's local closed-source files only. Revit 2008 to 2013 files open and report their release, metadata and schema. Revit 2011 to 2014 projects export typed elements under Revit's ElementIds, on Revit's storeys, with doors and windows in their walls and named types and layer sets; checked against one 2013 sample saved by Revit 2015, not against Revit's export.

capabilities.name: Revit 2015 to 2018 partition element records, read in the 32-bit layout of Revit 2019 to 2023, with storeys, hosts, type names, layer sets and materials
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records_2023::REVIT_32BIT_RELEASES and schema_tags; partition_level_records::LEVEL_PLACEMENT_KIND_2015; partition_compound_structure::wall_orientation_has_word; partition_materials::pattern_slots_32; partition_names::find_element_data_names_32; probes/examples/probe_re181_revit_2015_2018.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-181-revit-2015-2018-element-records.md; reports/element-framing/RE-198-revit-2015-bimcollab-export.md
capabilities.notes: Revit 2015 to 2018 frame their element records as 2019 does (RE-180): on Autodesk's 2016 to 2018 sample projects every record marker but 4 to 109 per file (as many as on the 2019 copy, but 15 on 2016 rst_basic) has a declared u32 ElementId 52 bytes before it, and so do all but 4 to 6 per file of Autodesk's six 2015 sample projects (pinned by #801) and 0 to 68 per file of three of its 2015 templates; 2014 is not read, since the one 2014 file measured is not documented. Each release takes its own tags of the five schema classes RE-180 lists. Three layouts differ from 2019's: a Level record's placement kind is 0xffffef6f, a wall's flip follows its location line with no word between (as on 2019 and 2020), and a material's shading frame holds two pattern slots, not four. On 2015 to 2018 a type's element-data name is looked for in its own data only and a one-unit entry is passed over. Revit's own export is measured on one 2015 project, BIMcollab's structural example (RE-198, a public download): all 241 of its elements by ElementId, in Revit's class or IFC4's for its IFC2X3 one, 3 written that the export leaves out (#879), and none of its elements' GlobalIds Revit's (#878). On rac_basic, rst_basic and rac_advanced of 2016 to 2018 every ElementId shared with the 2019 copy has its class; 2018 rac_basic and rac_advanced agree on every field, and the other differences are in the files' own bytes (boxes, reference lists, 2016's shading colours, 2016 rst_basic's renamed families). On five of the six 2015 sample projects every ElementId shared with the 2019 copy has its class; the sixth, rst_basic, shares no ElementId with it (another model), and the differing fields (type materials from RE-82's scan, renamed families, curtain-wall member boxes) are counted in RE-181 §6, not explained. Not read, as on 2019 to 2023: design options, layered joins, IFC export overrides, parameters.

capabilities.name: Furniture, casework, fixtures, equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall parts, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes from partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PRODUCT_RECORD_CATEGORIES; tests/element_records_2025.rs against Drshelden/IFC-ECS RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (MIT, fetched by CI tier 2); probes/examples/probe_re33_category_census.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-33-product-categories.md
capabilities.notes: Thirteen more BuiltInCategory values decode under the unchanged RE-21 instance rule, and every ElementId they select from a record carrying it at +0x00 is a Tag in Revit's own export of the same file: zero false positives on RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing (Revit 2025) and on Snowdon Towers (Revit 2024, measured locally). With RE-35's second-prologue ids, RE1 Architecture exports all 58 elements of these categories, RE1 Mechanical all 66 ducts, pipes and fittings and RE1 Plumbing all 117 pipes and fittings and all 6 fixtures, plus one fixture Revit's export leaves out; on Snowdon, curtain panels, railings, ceilings, furniture and fixtures are complete, and 47 curtain panels are elements Revit's export omits (#309). The 60 placed instances with no 3D volume are left out as Revit leaves them out. Second-prologue frames keep the container and placement fields, so the unattributed count covers placed instances only and matches the missing elements exactly for pipes, fittings, mullions, columns, railings, ceilings and furniture. Bodies are the record bounding box; entities are the IFC4 types (IfcFurniture, IfcSanitaryTerminal, IfcCovering, IfcMember, IfcPlate, IfcRailing, IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcDuctSegment, IfcDuctFitting, IfcPipeSegment, IfcPipeFitting). Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Revit 2024 and 2025 projects export furniture, casework, plumbing fixtures, specialty equipment, ceilings, curtain-wall mullions and panels, railings, wall sweeps, ducts and pipes whose records carry their ElementId, each one an element Revit's own export also holds; the diagnostics count the rest.

capabilities.name: ElementIds for second-prologue partition element records, read from the enclosing partition record
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::partition_record_chain / assign_second_prologue_ids / RevitFile::second_prologue_ids; tests/partition_record_chain.rs (every first-prologue frame starts a record of its own id on Core Interior and the RE1 models); tests/element_records_2025.rs; probes/examples/probe_re35_record_wrapper.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-35-partition-record-wrapper.md; reports/element-framing/RE-43-invalid-element-id.md
capabilities.notes: Every Partitions/* stream opens with a chain of records, one per element: u64 ElementId, u32 size, u16 prologue constant (release constant + 28), u16 count, the body, and a 16-byte trailer that repeats the size (RE-35). A first-prologue frame starts its record; a second-prologue frame (RE-30) sits inside its element's record, so its ElementId is the record's, read rather than inferred. All 30,432 first-prologue frames across nine 2024 and 2025 files start a record of their own id, and the chains hold every declared id on Core Interior and the RE1 models. Records after the chain belong to loaded families' own documents and never export. Against Revit's own exports: RE1 Architecture, Mechanical and Plumbing reach 100% of every recovered entity; Snowdon Towers Architectural exports 6,045 elements, 5,945 in Revit's export (a frame holding u32::MAX, the invalid ElementId, also takes its record's id, RE-43), with every wall, column, door, window, curtain wall and panel, railing, ceiling, furniture item, fixture and generic model of Revit's export attributed once RE-41 declares the ElemTable's second id. The rest are real elements Revit's export leaves out (#309); the 18 in non-primary design options are left out as Revit leaves them out (RE-40). Floors, building pads and ceilings get their ids too. It replaces RE-34's reference-order inference, which gave a door its type's id on a Revit 2025 file outside its hold-outs. Placed instances with no 3D volume are left out, as Revit leaves them out. Revit 2024 and 2025 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Files whose element records mostly lack an ElementId at their start (Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples, the RE1 models, projects saved incrementally) export their walls, doors, windows, floors, ceilings, columns, curtain-wall parts, railings, furniture, fixtures, ducts and pipes under the ElementIds Revit itself uses; the diagnostics count what is still left out.

capabilities.name: ElemTable records whose two ids differ declare the second
capabilities.evidence: elem_table::declared_ids; probes/examples/probe_re41_elem_table_secondary_ids.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-41-elem-table-secondary-ids.md
capabilities.notes: A 40-byte Global/ElemTable record carries two u32 ids, at +16 and +36. They agree on every record of Core Interior, the RE1 models, teste_export_2025, Projeto1 and the 2016-2023 projects measured. On Autodesk's Snowdon Towers samples (local only) they differ on 84 records (Architectural) and 27 (Structural); there the second is the id of the element's partition record (RE-35) and the Tag Revit's own IFC export writes, and the first is neither. The element's property set gains TypeName. Every name written equals the type half of Revit's ObjectType for the same Tag: 460 on Core Interior (360 walls, 99 floors, the pad), 1,545 on Snowdon Towers Architectural, 16 on RE1 Architecture, 1 on Projeto1, and 6 of 7 on teste_export_2025, where the seventh wall's frame, data and bounding box all describe the other type, so that export was made from a later state of the model. Types with no element-data block stay unnamed: RE1's one railing type and 7 of 22 Snowdon railing types. capabilities.user_impact: Walls, curtain walls, doors, windows, slabs, roofs, columns, beams, coverings, railings, stairs, ramps, proxies and spaces say whether they are external, as in Revit's own export, which energy and code-checking tools read.

capabilities.notes: Revit's exporter (revit-ifc IFC_v24.3.40, read and cited) reads a parameter named <set>.<property> on the element before anything else for that property, and writes a common set where its IFC4 definition applies it to the element's entity. rvt-rs reads each such parameter of a property listed in standard_property_sets (IFC4's 278 property sets that apply to an entity, generated from buildingSMART's IFC4 definitions as its validation service lists them, with IFC4's entity hierarchy, #817) from the element's own data object, by how it is stored: a Yes/No or integer as the u32 after its key, a text as u32 n · UTF-16 after it, a number as the f64 just before it (a length in feet, a thermal transmittance in W/(m²·K)). Booleans, identifiers, labels, text, counts, integers, lengths and thermal transmittance are read; angles, areas, ratios, enumerations and a type's parameters are not. Each is written in its set on the element, where the set applies to the entity written, as the type IFC4 declares, replacing rvt-rs's own value. Measured on the BIM4LCA office, the only model measured that defines such parameters: every value Revit's export writes from them is on the element itself; as built, property values equal to Revit's go from 14,531 to 18,374 and at building permit from 14,501 to 18,373, and the 7 stair values that differed are now Revit's; 55 OccupancyNumber values differ in type only (IFC4's IfcCountMeasure, the export's IfcInteger). That export, IFC4 Reference View, also used a user-defined property set file: its glazing set on 846 walls, curtain walls and coverings, its Pset_SpaceCommon covering texts and the absence of IsWired come from it and are not reproduced, and rvt-rs writes IsWired, a stored 0, as No on the doors and windows that carry it, where the export writes none. Revit 2024 files only, among those measured.
capabilities.user_impact: Fire and acoustic ratings, load bearing, U-values, glazing, handicap access and stair dimensions that a Revit model keeps in parameters named for IFC properties reach the IFC in their standard sets, as in Revit's own export.

capabilities.notes: Revit's four IFC export parameters are entries i64 BuiltInParameter, u32 n, UTF-16 value in an element's serialised data: IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_AS (-1019014), IFC_EXPORT_ELEMENT_TYPE_AS (-1019015), IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE (-1019016) and IFC_EXPORT_PREDEFINEDTYPE_TYPE (-1019017), public BuiltInParameter values. An entry belongs, on Revit 2024 and later, to the declared element whose data object (RE-153) holds it, and on earlier releases to the declared element whose element-data header (RE-44) is the last one before it, at most 0x800 bytes back (0x1ac measured); on the BIM4LCA office's permit file the header rule gave IfcSpace to doors, curtain walls, sketch lines and five drains (RE-190); a value must have the shape of an IFC entity name or an enumerator. An element exports as its own override, else its type's (IfcCoveringType naming IfcCovering), with its own predefined type, else its type's, written only when it is an IFC4 enumerator of that entity. RE1, Snowdon Towers, Einhoven and Projeto1 carry no export parameter. The owners of IfcShadingDevice equal RE-22's owner-offset read, which no longer feeds the export. IfcSpace and IfcFooting overrides exist on Core only on elements Revit does not export and stay unhonoured. Revit's own category-to-entity mapping table is not read, and no IfcSlabType or IfcCoveringType is written. Revit 2024's exporter does not act on a curtain wall's value (RE-188) or, measured on the BIM4LCA office only, a wall sweep's (RE-192), so a 2024 file's curtain walls and wall sweeps keep their class. Revit 2024 and 2025.

capabilities.notes: A structural-framing element's data carries its location line as a bounded line record: 04 00 08 01, start and end parameters (f64 ft), an origin (3 f64, model ft) and a unit direction (3 f64), found in the data up to the next element-data header. With the element's record box, beam_body solves a box length x width x depth along the line: the length is the line's, the depth comes from the vertical extent, the width from one plan extent, and the other plan extent must come out to 0.01 ft. A level beam exports as Extrusion::rectangle(length, width, depth) rotated to the line's plan angle; a sloped one keeps its record box as the extrusion and sweeps its section along its centreline (SolidShape::SweptPath, IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid with +Z as the fixed reference). On Snowdon Towers Structural (local only) all 942 exported framing elements carry a line, 940 inside their box, and 923 solve (802 level on a model axis, 111 level rotated in plan, 10 sloped); IfcOpenShell meshes each exported solid to its record box (938 to 0.001 ft, 4 to 0.0016 ft). Against the meshes of the 2027 edition's VIM export, scored only where that edition kept the beam's Location, type and mesh consistent (839), the section across the line equals Revit's on 613 and Revit's less the top a floor join cuts on 179; the ends equal Revit's on 485 and Revit trims 352 at their supports (median 0.625 ft at the larger end), which is not read. Rotated beams' solids are 1.108 times Revit's own beam envelope at the median, against 8.406 times for the record box they replace. Status is partial: ends are not trimmed, floor-join cuts are not applied, the section is a rectangle envelope, 17 beams (15 oblique with skewed ends) keep their box, and no licensed CI file has structural framing. Revit 2024 only.
capabilities.user_impact: Beams, joists and girders export along their own axes instead of as boxes around them, so a diagonal beam is a beam, not a slab of the bay it crosses. Since RE-103 a steel beam whose type stores an I section is that I (IfcIShapeProfileDef), flanges across and web upright: 377 of Snowdon Towers' 942 framing elements, and on all 271 its VIM export can score, Revit's own mesh has the section's corners, flange tips and web faces where rvt-rs puts them. Channels, angles, joists and concrete beams keep their box along the line. Since RE-104 a structural column whose type stores an I section is that I turned to the column's own X axis: all 40 of Snowdon Towers' steel columns, and Revit's own mesh on all 24 its VIM export can score. Since RE-105 each of those 417 members is written with an IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage whose IfcMaterialProfile pairs its type's material with its I. Since RE-221 a column whose type is a square hollow section is that section, rounded corners and all (IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids over IfcIndexedPolyCurves, as Revit writes it), read from its family's parameters b, Ht, t and kr: Revit's body on all 79 such columns of the BIM4LCA office as built and 55 at building permit.

capabilities.notes: A pipe's two ends are connector entries in its partition: a u64 element, a u32 connector index, the u32 1 and three f64 (model ft). The entry's element is the pipe itself or the element connected at that end (pipe 442026's two ends are keyed by two fittings placed 0.1413 ft beyond them), so an entry is found by where its point falls in the pipe's box. The record box gives the outside radius by cylinder-box inversion (jakobhirn-bit, Discussion #112): every axis that is not nearly the pipe's own must give the same radius (to 0.002 ft), and the box rebuilt from the cylinder must be the record box on all six sides (to 0.002 ft), or the pipe keeps its box. Exported as a PlacedExtrusion over IfcCircleProfileDef, BodySource partition_pipe_axis. Measured on GitHub's runners (Measure run 36723473598) against Revit's own IFC on the MIT RE1 models: 69 of 69 pipes (Mechanical 6, Plumbing 63) are circle-profile extrusions with Revit's radius, axis ends and length to 0.00001 ft; main drew every one as a box and had the right axis for 23 of the 69 (21 of Plumbing's 63, 2 of Mechanical's 6). No other model's IFC changes. Revit 2024 (#869): the BIM4LCA office's 12 pipes, on both its as-built and building-permit files, are circle-profile extrusions with Revit's radius, axis ends and length to 0.00001 ft (Measure run 40146906605; Revit writes their profile as four arcs, which tools/re/pipe_bodies_vs_ifc.py reads), and their 24 ports sit at their ends within 0.01 ft with Revit's axis. A 2024 pipe has no inner diameter read, so it writes no InvertElevation rather than one taken from its axis alone. Status is partial: Revit 2024 and 2025 only (jakobhirn-bit reads the same entries on 2026, on files that cannot run in CI), every measured pipe runs along a principal axis so sloped pipes rest on the rebuild proof and not on an oracle, and ducts and pipe fittings keep their boxes.

capabilities.notes: A duct's or pipe's object lists its connectors' joins after its RbsCurveConnectorManager anchor, as counted lists of two references (the curve's connector and the one joined: a u64 element, a u32 connector index, the u32 1). A join is written in two blocks; the earlier block stores the curve's own connector index inverted, so a list in the later block is read as stored and one in the earlier block inverted when no later list gives the join. RE-141: a fitting's joins are written in the same list form with the fitting as the first reference, and are found by the list alone anywhere in a partition (a fitting's own record holds only the ascending ids it refers to, with no connector index; the pipes' connector managers are not in the leading record chain). A fitting's list is written once with its own connector index as Revit numbers it (a tee's are 1, 2 and 3), where a duct's or pipe's earlier copy is inverted. Every duct and pipe written as a distribution element has a port at each end (B54), and a family instance one for each connector of its symbol, cable tray and conduit ones aside (RE-169); every port is nested in its element with an IfcRelNests, one per element, as Revit's own IFC4 export nests them, a proxy's too (B83, B84). RE-197: a port's PredefinedType is its connector's domain (DUCT, CABLE or PIPE; a duct's or pipe's DUCT or PIPE) and NOTDEFINED for an undefined domain, as Revit's IFC4 export types it, and a connector of a domain Revit's exporter gives no direction, all but HVAC and piping, is SOURCEANDSINK (revit-ifc ConnectorExporter). RE-212: an HVAC or piping connector's direction is the Flow Direction its family sets in the connector's parameters or, where the family leaves it bidirectional, the one Revit calculated for the instance's connector, and a duct's or pipe's is its calculated one; those ports are named InPort_, OutPort_ or Port_ by it and described Flow, as Revit's export names them, and every one of the RE1 models' 463 ports has Revit's FlowDirection. SystemType, the connector's system classification, is not read. Measured on GitHub's runners (Measure run 39261416282) against Revit's own exports: all 73 of RE1 Mechanical's port-to-port connections and all 126 of Plumbing's are written, with none and 2 not in Revit's export, and every one of Revit's 150 and 260 ports, each tied to its element, with no schema finding; on the BIM4LCA office all 67 ports have Revit's PredefinedType and 43 its FlowDirection, and all 53 of RE1 Electrical's are SOURCEANDSINK, as in Revit's export. No port takes a direction Revit's export does not give it. Status is partial: every port's SystemType and an electrical connector's description, the Flow=Source or Flow=Sink Revit's exporter writes, are not read (#834). #869: a port joined to a placed duct or pipe port takes that port's point and Z axis, as Revit's export places every port joined to a segment's: within 0.01 ft of Revit's on all 118 such ports of RE1 Plumbing and all 59 of RE1 Mechanical, axes as Revit's on 108 and 53 and opposite on 10 and 6. Every other family-instance port is placed at its connector: the m_trf of its m_arrConnectorData entry in the symbol that draws the instance (InstanceInfo.m_symbolId, RE-215), whose m_or is the point and the third column of whose m_3x3 is the Z axis, through the instance's transform (RE-87). On Revit 2025 all 53 such ports of RE1 Electrical, 29 of Mechanical and 18 of Plumbing are within 0.01 ft of Revit's, with Revit's axis (Measure 40116733274), and on Revit 2024 all 43 of the BIM4LCA office's (Measure 40141465973, scored in each file's own site frame, since Revit writes the office's site at its shared coordinates); taking the type's symbol instead put 9 of Plumbing's and 2 of Mechanical's up to 0.81 ft off, since fittings sized per instance have symbols of their own.
capabilities.user_impact: Ducts, pipes, fittings and family instances carry IfcDistributionPort connections: all 73 of Revit's export's connections on RE1 Mechanical and all 126 on Plumbing, with every one of Revit's 150 and 260 ports. capabilities.notes: A roof's OST_SketchLines records carry the roof's ElementId as their owner reference, as a floor's do (RE-25), and close into its plan outline under the same box solve. A sketch line's element data also carries the bounded line record RE-49 reads for beams (04 00 08 01, start and end parameters, origin, unit direction), so its exact ends are known. Where the box solve does not close an element, its lines' recorded ends are chained into loops, provided every line is level with both ends in its own record's box and every end is shared by exactly two lines; otherwise the element keeps no profile. Profiles that closed before are unchanged, except that an element whose box-solved outline uses a line that reads as an arc, a quarter arc whose ends are two corners of its box, is read from its lines' curves instead (RE-96 §4, #824): the BIM4LCA office's roof 1461758 then has Revit's outline, 61 of the office's 63 slab outlines (59 at building permit) within 0.01 ft of Revit's. Measured on Snowdon Towers Architectural (local only) per Tag against the upward-face plan area of Revit's own IFC4 geometry (IfcOpenShell 0.8.5): 13 of 20 roofs carry an outline (none did), 6 equal to Revit's area, 5 equal per layer (Revit writes layered roofs as stacked layer solids) and 2 larger (5.4% and 34.7%, cut in Revit's geometry); every roof outline's plan box is its record box. Slabs rise from 117 to 132 of 199 with an outline (149 since RE-96, below); the 15 added are 11 equal (4 outright, 7 per layer) and 4 larger by 0.2% to 3.0%, the shaft-opening residual earlier outlines also show. RE-56: each roof sketch line's data carries its edge's slope angle (9:12 by default) and flags (00 00 01 00, or 01 01 01 00 on an edge that defines the slope, followed by -rise/run); a roof type's layers follow its name and u32 0. A 2024 roof with exactly one defining edge is drawn rising from it at its slope with its type's thickness square to the slope, as an IfcFacetedBrep, only when that reproduces its record box height within 1e-4 ft: on the Autodesk tutorial house (local only) the one sloped roof, 1:12 over 20.458 ft with a 1.25 ft type, gives 2.9591938797 ft against the recorded 2.959193880 ft. RE-199 (puzzbobb, #870): on Revit 2025 the same edge block holds at +0x3b how far the edge's plane is raised rather than -rise/run, a sketch line's data holds its segment as on 2024, and a Sketch lists its curves as RE-97 found; a roof with several defining edges is drawn as its edges' planes, each held to its straight-skeleton wedge, the eave set by the shallowest edge; a slope arrow's SlopeCurveData (tail and head heights, angle, set by height or by slope) slopes a roof with no defining edge; a 2025 ProfileRoof's rafter cut (parameter -1001710) and fascia depth are read, and a two-cut is cut level at its eave. Each body is drawn only where it reproduces the record box height within 1e-4 ft. On puzzbobb's 23 Revit 2025 models (R2025_Models.zip, Apache-2.0, Measure -f r2025=true, run 39602093604) 18 of the 19 roofs in Revit's exports match Revit's body, every vertex within 0.001 ft and the volume within 1e-4 (main: 0 of 19); the 19th is a roof by extrusion (#883). RE-211 reads a 2025 roof by extrusion's sketch, a clamped B-spline (or lines) in a vertical plane that is the roof's top, offsets it square by the type's thickness for the underside, cuts both ends plumb and runs it across the record box, kept only where it reproduces the record box to 0.001 ft: on the R2025 model 11_RoofByExtrusion all 1,187 of Revit's vertices are within 0.001 ft of the section and its volume is 1.00015 times Revit's (Measure run 40003971692). On Autodesk's samples (no Revit export) rac_advanced's slope-arrow roof is drawn in its 2024 and 2025 saves, its three 15-degree hips are read on 2025 but fail the record-box check and stay level, and 29, 4 and 1 more elements of rac_advanced, rac_basic and rst_basic 2025 take their sketch outline. Status is partial: roofs by extrusion outside Revit 2025 (only one, on 2025, is measured), hip roofs over a T or U footprint (#884), a square two-cut with a fascia, and roofs sloped some other way (Snowdon's 2112673 has no defining edge but is sloped in Revit's export) stay level plates of their record box's height; a 2024 roof with several defining edges takes the RE-199 path but none is measured (#885); cuts are not subtracted, 7 roofs keep their box, and the recorded ends are read on Revit 2024 and 2025 only. RE-96: a sketch line's curve can be an arc in RE-75's layout without the u64 1 that marks a wall's arc; it counts where every point of it, drawn as chords within 0.0005 ft, lies in the line's record box and the record does not also hold as a line, and an outline with an arc is kept only where it spans its element's record box within 0.001 ft. On Snowdon Towers 17 more slabs carry an outline (132 to 149 of 199): 14 within 0.1% of Revit's upward-face area, 2 half of it (Revit writes each as two solids) and 1 0.8% larger (a tessellated face set in Revit's export); slabs within 0.1% go from 73 to 87. RE-97: a Sketch element's data names the sketched element at +77 and lists its curves (u32 n, n x (u64 id, u32 key), keys rising, with gaps where curves were deleted); where a sketch's list differs from the lines whose owner reference names the element (55 of 447 on Snowdon Towers), the list is the membership, and the outline is kept only where it spans the element's record box. On Snowdon 176 of 199 slabs and all 20 roofs carry an outline (149 and 13 before); slabs within 0.1% of Revit's upward-face area go from 89 to 102 and roofs from 7 to 10 (plan_profiles_vs_ifc.py now takes every piece with one Tag together, which re-scores main from 87 to 89). RE-98: ceilings take their sketch's outline through the same path. Measured on each element's top surface (Revit writes a layered ceiling as one stacked solid per layer, each with the outline): 66 of Snowdon Towers' 68 ceilings within 0.1% of Revit's area (50 before, the rectangles their box already drew), and all 6 of RE1 Architecture's (Revit 2025, 5 before). RE-99: shaft openings (OST_ShaftOpening, -2000996) are sketched as floors are, their sketches holding the two crossing diagonals Revit draws in plan besides the boundary; without those, 8 of Snowdon's 9 shafts close, and each is cut as a void from the one-piece floors, roofs and ceilings within its height that hold it strictly inside: 7 elements on Snowdon, all closer to Revit's area (2 slabs now exact). A shaft on an element's edge, which Revit cuts as a notch, is not cut. Measured on each element's top surface, 150 of Snowdon's slabs are within 0.1% of Revit's area. RE-100: a sketch line that is a full circle is stored in the arc layout under tag 04 00 08 00 with both angles 0; shaft 903725 is one, and read it cuts its round void from 5 more elements, taking Snowdon's slabs within 0.1% of Revit's area to 154.

capabilities.notes: A straight run's element data holds its plan sketch as bounded line records (04 00 08 01) at its base elevation: two boundary lines from the first riser to the last, then a line across the run at each riser. The run type its reference list names (OST_StairsRuns type definition) has a serialised object 01 00 00 00 + u64 id with tag db 0f at +0x47, structural depth, tread thickness, riser thickness and nosing length as f64 ft at +0x59, +0x69, +0x71, +0x79, flags monolithic / treads / risers / slanted risers at +0xbd..+0xc0, a flag at +0xb5 set on the one type whose treads run under the riser above, then its name. With the stair's riser height (RE-47) the run's side view is extruded across it as an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid with a stated Position. Measured on Snowdon Towers (local only) against Revit's IFC4 and a VIM: 34 of 43 runs drawn; the 30 steel-pan runs equal Revit's geometry to 1e-5 ft; the 4 with upright risers square the nosing Revit shapes with a nosing profile, and one runs its first riser short of Revit's below a landing. RE-92: a run's data holds the StairsRun fields in schema order, seven f64 (bottom elevation, top elevation, extend below base, extend below tread base, run width, stringer widths), u32 top riser index, then flags centre mark, begin with riser, end with riser; it is read where the bottom elevation and width equal the sketch's. End with riser is 0 on exactly the three runs with one riser line more than risers; such a run's last tread runs to the last riser line. Monolithic runs with slanted risers are drawn as one body with one riser fewer than riser lines, the underside the type's structural depth square to the pitch below the inner corners, cut by the floor. 38 of 43 runs drawn; the 4 added equal Revit's geometry but for the upright run's nosing edge. Riserless and spiral runs keep their record box. Run type names equal the type part of Revit's ObjectType on all 49 exported flights. RE-217 (Revit 2025): the byte anchors are absent, so a run's sketch, riser height and ends are read by member name from its native records (StairsRun m_actualRunWidth, m_bottomElevation, m_beginWithRiser, m_endWithRiser; one StairsTreadInfo per tread, m_origin, m_actDepth, m_runDirProj, m_riserDir, m_runType), its construction from its StairsRunType record, and its type from its element record's reference list as on 2024, which equals Revit's flight type on all 75 runs measured (the R2025 stair models and both BIM4LCA office files). capabilities.notes: Global/History lists every editing episode's GUID newest first (u32 count at +0x0e, a u32-counted table at +0x66, then the count again and count entries of a Windows-order GUID and the byte 0x28); a 40-byte Global/ElemTable record holds its element's episode number at +0x18, whose GUID is entry count-1-episode. The GlobalId is that GUID with the record's first ElementId XORed into its last 32 bits (an element whose id has since changed, RE-41, keeps its first), in IFC base-64. Per Tag against Revit's own exports, every element rvt-rs exports that Revit's holds has Revit's GlobalId: Core Interior 854 of 854, RE1 Architecture/Mechanical/Plumbing/Electrical 73/73/123/12, teste_export_2025 8, Projeto1 2, Snowdon Towers 5,945 of 5,945 (local only), with no duplicate GlobalId in any export. Revit's own synthesised parts (stair components, a ramp's flight, extra slab pieces) have GlobalIds of Revit's making and are not written by rvt-rs; a Tag carried by several rvt-rs entities gives the rebuilt GlobalId to the first only. Revit 2023 and earlier (28-byte ElemTable records) keep generated GlobalIds, as do openings, further pieces of an element, relationships and property sets. RE-220 (#878): the project, site and building take the GlobalIds the file stores, which Revit's export writes: under IFC_PROJECT_GUID, IFC_SITE_GUID and IFC_BUILDING_GUID (-1019002, -1019004, -1019003) on BIMcollab's Revit 2015 example, and as an untagged triple related as revit-ifc's fake ElementIds -16, -15 and -14 relate them (site = project XOR 2, building = project XOR 1) on both BIM4LCA office files: 3 of 3 on each where 0 were. A storey takes the IFC_GUID value its Level's id stands twice before, 58 bytes apart: BIMcollab's 5 of 5 storeys, where none were. A file that stores none keeps generated project, site and building GlobalIds: their base GUID is none of the elements', the history's or BasicFileInfo's (measured negative). Since #400 a generated GlobalId is a SHA-256 of a fixed namespace, the document's Unique Document GUID and the entity's own identity (ElementId and piece, filling element, participants), never its position in the file: Snowdon Towers exported before and after RE-75's curved walls keeps all 20,149 GlobalIds (7,740 before #400). Status is partial: Revit 2023 and earlier, the project, site and building of a file that stores none, and storeys whose Level is not recovered keep generated GlobalIds. Where it applies it is exact against Revit's own exports of two releases (Core Interior 2024; RE1 2025), CI-gated.
capabilities.user_impact: An IFC file from rvt-rs and Revit's own IFC of the same model name every element, room and storey with the same GlobalId, so diffs line up and BCF issues, clash results and federated links carry over between them.

capabilities.name: Door and Window host-wall binding from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::decode_reference_list + partition_schema_mvp::opening_instances_from_records; tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_door_window_host_wall_binding compares the emitted (host wall, opening) pairs against the reference export's own IfcRelVoidsElement + IfcRelFillsElement chain and requires exact set equality (138/138, 0 wrong, 0 missing); the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict carries relations.IFCRELFILLSELEMENT inside the claimed surface, where rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell 0.8.5 and IFClite 7.1.1 emit byte-identical 138-pair sets
capabilities.notes: Scope is two BuiltInCategories (OST_Doors, OST_Windows), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. The carrier is a counted reference list that follows the element record's bounding box: a u32 length at +0x88 and that many u64 slots at +0x8c. The host is the slot immediately before the record's own ElementId, accepted only when it is one of the 360 ElementIds the RE-21 instance rule selects as exported walls, so a wrong read fails closed instead of inventing a host. Measured on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt: 273 of 273 door/window records give the correct host, and the emitted IfcRelFillsElement pair set equals Revit's own exactly - 138 of 138, no wrong host, no missing pair, no extra pair. Three fixed-shape readings were rejected and are recorded in RE-23: u64 at +0xac is right on 186 of 273 records, u64 at +0xa4 on 81, and 'the last two slots are (host, self)' on 192 - the list length varies (6 on every door record, 18 on every window record, up to 101 elsewhere) and 81 door records continue past their own id with a trailing type-symbol slot. The predecessor read is not a category discriminator: 528 of 638 wall records also have a wall predecessor, which is why the rule is applied only to the two categories RE-21 already identifies by BuiltInCategory. Emission is the IFC4 chain Revit uses - IfcOpeningElement (bodied with the door/window's own record bounding box, placed on the element's placement, not a wall-relative cut) plus IfcRelVoidsElement and IfcRelFillsElement. The opening's Tag repeats the filling element's, which is what the reference export does on all 138. The export's other 63 IfcOpeningElement - 42 in slabs, 20 in shading devices, 1 unfilled wall penetration - are not recovered: rvt-rs emits no opening that is not filled by a recovered element. This is not evidence for any other category or release. Outside that scope, on Snowdon Towers (2024, local only), the slot before the record's own id gave Revit's host for 107 doors and windows. The list is in ascending ElementId order, so since RE-85 the host is the nearest exported wall the list names below the record's own id, then above it, skipping curtain walls: 192 of the 194 doors and windows Revit fills an opening for take its host and the other 2 another wall Revit also cuts; Core Interior stays 138 of 138 (#439). Since RE-83 the opening is cut to the host wall's depth: within 0.25 ft of Revit's opening on all 138 Core Interior openings. Since RE-84 a door or window whose type draws no geometry (a type value block with no geometry-material map) is written as its opening alone, voiding its host with no filler, as Revit writes it: 48 of 48 such elements on Snowdon Towers, Core Interior and RE1 Architecture are opening-only in Revit's export.
capabilities.user_impact: Doors and windows come out of a Revit 2024 project as IFC4 fills of a real host wall, so a viewer subtracts the opening from the wall and shows the door in it - matching Revit's own export relationship for relationship.

capabilities.evidence: element_record_plan_profiles::plan_profiles_from_sketch_line_records wired through partition_schema_mvp::slabs_from_partition_category_records; reports/element-framing/RE-25-slab-plan-profiles.md; partition_schema_mvp::sketch_plan_profiles (RE-50 recorded ends, RE-95 zero-length lines); probes/examples/probe_re95_zero_length_sketch_lines.rs; tools/re/plan_profiles_vs_ifc.py; reports/element-framing/RE-95-zero-length-sketch-lines.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_slab_plan_profiles (all 100 record-backed plates resolve a profile; the 20 28-vertex rings with a void are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set) plus the unit gates in src/research/element_record_plan_profiles.rs; partition_beam_axes::scan_first_records (Copies::Current for sketch scans); partition_schema_mvp::current_sketch_records; element_record_plan_profiles::sketch_curve_list_copies / scan_sketch_curve_lists; probes/examples/probe_824_sketch_lists.rs; probes/examples/probe_824_slab_arcs.rs; reports/element-framing/RE-216-current-instance-copies.md
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 floor slab exports with the polygon its sketch actually encloses - including its voids - instead of the bounding rectangle, so a courtyard ring comes out as a ring.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_SketchLines, -2000045), one release band (Revit 2024), one recorded edge, and only the plates the RE-22 instance rule already recovers. The join is exact and byte-anchored: the last slot of the second counted reference list at +0x88 names the sketched element, and the 3688 sketch-line records on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt name 126 owners including all 80 exported IFCSLAB and all 20 exported IFCSHADINGDEVICE ids. No geometry takes part in the join. The reconstruction is a closure rule over the recorded segment bounding boxes, not a fit: a box degenerate on one axis contributes its endpoints, every other box is placed only when exactly one pair of still-open vertices fits it, and an ambiguous segment, a vertex that does not finish at degree 2, an unused edge, a zero-extent box or a loop under three vertices rejects the whole element. Measured against Revit's own export (IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, project plan frame, cyclic sequences with orientation normalised, tolerance 1e-3 ft per vertex): 80 of 80 slab profiles exact across 122 loops - 80 outer plus 42 rectangular voids - worst vertex deviation 1.563e-12 ft, and 2.842e-14 ft re-measured on the emitted IFC after the metre round-trip. 42 perimeter plates emit IFCARBITRARYPROFILEDEFWITHVOIDS (26-vertex outer ring, one rectangular void) and 38 emit IFCARBITRARYCLOSEDPROFILEDEF. Status is partial rather than verified because that agreement is measured and regression-gated but is not a field of either OctetProof claimed surface: no witness compares profile geometry, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. The 20 exported IFCSHADINGDEVICE are plates whose 57 sketch-line boxes include one of zero extent and 21 diagonals with no axis-parallel anchor, which the box closure declines. RE-95: the zero-extent record is a zero-length segment with no bounded line whose point ends two of the others; left out, the other 56 lines' recorded ends (RE-50) close each plate into a 28-vertex ring with one void, and all 20 equal Revit's outline (upward-face area 0.00% off, every vertex within 0.001 ft, tools/re/plan_profiles_vs_ifc.py). The pre-RE-25 plan-loop scan is a measured dead end here: 2317 closed plan-polyline candidates across all eight inflated partitions, none with the plan bounds of any recovered plate, and no ordered vertex run of the export's polygon anywhere in the file at any stride. Walls, doors, windows and columns still carry the record bounding box; base/top Level ElementId binding stays open (#86). This is not evidence for any other category or release. A sketch of several separate loops is several pieces, each with the voids inside it; the exporter writes each further piece as another element with the element's Tag and a ':2', ':3' name suffix, as Revit's export does (#331): on Snowdon Towers (local only) the five such slabs match Revit's pieces. Loops that cross give no profile. Where a sketch line's, a sketch curve list's or the slab record's copies in several partitions disagree, the copy in the current partition is taken (RE-216 §8): the BIM4LCA permit file's slabs 1384047 and 1474132 then have Revit's outline, 61 of 63 slabs within 0.01 ft (Measure 40181361898).

capabilities.name: Wall body from Revit 2024 element records: run cut back by the joins the record names, plus thin-axis thickness
capabilities.evidence: element_record_wall_joins::joined_walls and ::join_trims wired through partition_schema_mvp::wall_instances_from_records; reports/element-framing/RE-26-world-coordinate-residuals.md and reports/element-framing/RE-29-join-reference-list.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_wall_join_trimmed_bodies (360 of 360 walls resolve, 322 take a trim), ::core_interior_2024_wall_joins_are_named_in_the_reference_list, the unit gates in src/research/element_record_wall_joins.rs including the_surviving_side_of_a_true_l_corner_is_still_over_trimmed, and the pinned ObjectPlacement x Position composition of wall 20800 in tools/ci/ifc_schema_arity.py
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 wall exports at the length its joins actually leave it, with the wall's real thickness, instead of the untrimmed centreline-to-centreline box - and the join partners are read out of the file rather than inferred from geometry alone.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Walls, -2000011), one release band (Revit 2024), one recorded edge, and only axis-parallel walls - every wall on this file is axis-parallel, and a box with no distinguishable thin plan axis is declined. Three measured facts back it. First, the box's thin plan extent is the wall's thickness: on the newest frame of each element it equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 walls. Second, every non-zero delta between the box and Revit's Axis polyline over all 720 wall ends is exactly 0.25, 0.3333 or 0.75 ft - half of the 6-inch, 8-inch and 18-inch wall thicknesses on the file - and zero everywhere else, so an end is cut by half the thickness of the perpendicular recovered wall whose centreline lands on it. Third, since #274 (RE-29) a candidate must additionally be NAMED in this record's counted reference list at +0x88, and is tested for reach against its own cut-back run rather than its recorded one. All inputs are recorded bounding boxes and nothing is fitted; candidates disagreeing about their thickness decline the whole element, and a trim that would collapse the run declines it too. Measured against Revit's own export (world axis-aligned bounding box, max of the two corner deltas, tolerance 1e-3 ft; RE-26 used IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, RE-29 used tools/re/ifc_world_aabb.py, which reproduces every RE-26 table exactly): 336 of 360 walls exact at RE-26 and 351 of 360 after RE-29, up from 27 before either; correct wall ends 689 -> 703 (membership) -> 711 of 720; mean residual 0.2701 -> 0.0220 -> 0.0081 ft. Per element 15 walls improve, 345 are unchanged and 0 regress. Status is partial, not verified, for two reasons. The 9 ends still wrong are all over-trims at one side of a TRUE L CORNER - two walls whose runs both stop at the other's centreline with nothing continuing past, where Revit cuts exactly one of the pair. Two such corners exist on this file (one repeated on eight storeys) and no feature in the record orders the two sides: the survivor is the thicker wall once and an equal-thickness wall once, the x wall once and the y wall once, the higher ElementId once and the lower once, the longer run once and the shorter once, and the prologue flag words do not order them consistently either. The solver keeps cutting both rather than guessing, so the residual is recorded and pinned rather than hidden. And no witness compares body geometry, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. This models Revit's join cleanup on top of a carrier it does read; it does not read the per-pair butt/mitre decision itself. Emitted product counts, relations, storeys and the diagnostics sidecar are unchanged. This is not evidence for any other category or release.; RE-127 (2026-09-28): the joined-wall lists decide the 9 remaining ends, 720 of 720 ends and 360 of 360 walls exact

capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Columns, -2000100), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. The type join is exact and byte-anchored: the last slot before the record's own ElementId in the counted reference list at +0x88 that is itself an OST_Columns record carrying placement kind 0xffff8000 (the type-symbol envelopes of RE-21 section 5). All 256 exported columns have exactly one candidate before their own id and it is 5755 (Column_Sqaure : 24 inch x 24 inch), which is the IfcColumnType.Tag Revit's own export writes for every one of them. The join ships with a fail-closed guard: the type section and the instance plan envelope must agree to 1e-6 ft or the join is dropped and the element keeps its envelope with ProfileResolved false. RE-26 left the body residual open - 176 of 256 columns were world-exact and the 80 that were not had a body Revit cuts inset from the full prism, which no section can produce. #274 (RE-29) closes it from the same +0x88 list: a column record names the walls that cut it, and the exported body is the record prism minus the UNTRIMMED record prisms of those walls - 256 of 256 exact at a worst residual of 9.4e-13 ft and a mean of 0.0000 ft, against 176 of 256 at 0.5833 ft / 0.1217 ft before, with 80 improved, 176 unchanged and 0 regressed. Substituting the join-trimmed wall runs scores 190 of 256, so a wall runs its full recorded length into a column it cuts. element_record_column_cuts::difference_box is fail-closed: it answers only when the surviving material fills its own bounding box exactly by volume, which on this file is true on every one of the 80 columns whose box shrinks and false on every one of the 69 interior slots, Ls and crosses, so a decline never emits material Revit removed and the emitted solid is never larger on any axis than what Revit kept. Status stays partial because the section is still only the symbol's bounding box and the cut is still a box difference rather than a recovered solid, and because no witness compares profile or body geometry - the OctetProof claimed surface scores counts and relations, not shapes. The one emitted count that moves is IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE 9231 -> 9311, the new JoinCutWallCount provenance row per cut column; BodySource becomes partition_element_record_join_cut on those columns. capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Walls, -2000011), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. A Revit wall TYPE has the bbox-less RE-24 record shape - the 88-byte prologue and the ff ff ff ff ab 05 marker at +0x50 with no bounding box - and a third value of the RE-21 placement-kind word at +0x42, 0xffff8080, alongside a counted slot list starting at +0x56 that names the record's own id. First, nothing is emitted: no IFC entity, property or relation changes, tests/fixtures/synthetic-project.ifc is byte-identical, every committed OctetProof observation and verdict is untouched, and no count in either manifest moves. Second, no witness scores a wall-to-type relation, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. Separately and explicitly NOT claimed: compound layer thicknesses. capabilities.name: An element's saved parameters, named by the file's definitions, in rvt-elements and Python (RE-207)
capabilities.evidence: elements::parameters::saved_parameters_lossy / SavedParameters::entries_for over research::native_element_parameters::read; native_parameter_definitions::project (ParamDefFamType as ElementId); rvt-elements and rvt-py decoded_elements; tests/element_parameters.rs (RVT_NORDIC_LCA_DIR, RVT_PROJECT_CORPUS_DIR/r2025); probes/examples/probe_re207_element_parameters.rs; tools/re/element_parameters_vs_ifc.py; reports/element-framing/RE-207-element-parameters.md
capabilities.notes: Revit 2023 to 2027 files. Each element's parameters are read from its native record (native_document::extract): its typed parameter sets (m_pParamValueSet*), the family slots of its own FamilyParams (FamilyInstance.m_pInstParams, FamilySymbol.m_pParams) a definition resolves, and the native fields read as built-in parameters. A parameter is named by its definition's m_caption (family, shared, project and global parameters); built-in parameters keep their negative id and no name, since the built-in catalog is not shipped (#255). A family instance's type (m_masterSymbolId) adds the type parameters the instance does not hold; a family parameter whose definition is an instance parameter is taken from the instance only. Values are saved, not evaluated, in internal units, with the SI value of a length, area, volume or angle. Measured against Revit's own IFC4 exports: on the BIM4LCA office (Revit 2024) every parameter named <set>.<property> whose property Revit writes on the element holds Revit's value, 7,606 of 7,606 as built and 7,592 of 7,592 at building permit; the housing on terrain 27 of 27; on the R2025 models a window's FireRating is its type's Fire Rating, 18 of 18. Exports made without Revit's own property sets do not show the other parameters, so their values are not measured. Not read: a family's built-in slots (a window type's Width and Height), a wall's or floor's type parameters, formulas' evaluated values. Nothing new is written to IFC.
capabilities.user_impact: Scripts and the CLI can read the family, shared and project parameters a Revit 2023 to 2027 model saves on each element and its type, by name, with units.

capabilities.name: Revit's own property sets, one per parameter group, in rvt-ifc --revit-property-sets (RE-210)
capabilities.evidence: ifc::revit_property_sets::attach; IfcModel::type_property_sets (step_writer merges them into the type object's sets); rvt-ifc --revit-property-sets; tests/revit_property_sets.rs (RVT_NORDIC_LCA_DIR, RVT_PROJECT_CORPUS_DIR); probes/examples/probe_re210_revit_property_sets.rs; tools/re/revit_property_sets_vs_ifc.py; reports/element-framing/RE-210-revit-property-sets.md
capabilities.notes: Revit 2023 to 2027 files, with the option only. Each element's named saved parameters (RE-207) are written as revit-ifc's Release_25.x.x branch writes them with "Export Revit property sets" (ParameterUtil.CacheParametersForElement, PropertyUtil.CreateInternalRevitPropertySets, CreateRealPropertyByType; read and cited, not copied): one set per parameter group, named by Revit's English label for the group (Other for none), the IFC group left out, one parameter per name with its spaces removed in a group; the type's parameters in such sets on its type object, or on its elements with (Type) added where it has none. A Yes/No is an IfcBoolean, an integer with a spec an IfcInteger, a non-empty text an IfcText, a length, pipe or duct size an IfcLengthMeasure, an area, volume, angle (radians) or number its measure, an air flow, HVAC or piping pressure, apparent or electrical power, electrical potential or current an IfcVolumetricFlowRateMeasure, IfcPressureMeasure, IfcPowerMeasure, IfcElectricVoltageMeasure or IfcElectricCurrentMeasure in SI units (declared in the unit assignment when written), a material ElementId the material's name, a family type's '<family> : <type>' (the type's name alone where both are the same). Measured against Revit 2025's export of Autodesk's Snowdon Towers HVAC with Export Revit property sets (local only, not committed): 28,906 of 28,906 properties written (counted per element) are in the set of the same name, on the element or type object of the same Tag, with Revit's value; Revit writes 79,907 more, nearly all built-in parameters. On Snowdon Towers Architectural, 58,346 of 58,733; 369 are in sets Revit names with (Type) on 13 of its type objects, which follows from the order of its export, and 18 are curtain panels' type category, written before RE-210. Measured against Revit 2024's own export of the BIM4LCA office as built (common sets only): FireExit, written in Identity Data, equals Pset_DoorCommon and Pset_WindowCommon.FireExit on 498 of 498 doors and windows. Not written: built-in parameters (no name, #255), enumerations, other specs, (Type) names on exported type objects; the sets keep rvt-rs's own GlobalIds, not Revit's hashed ones.
capabilities.user_impact: An export can carry a model's family, shared and project parameters by name, grouped as Revit's own export with Revit property sets groups them.
